definition: The most important law of a place. Every other law has to respect it.
Brazil's Supreme Federal Court: the country's highest court. It decides whether laws and government acts respect the Constitution.
To cancel a decision so that it no longer counts.
Technology that identifies a person by comparing the face a camera records with photos stored in a database.
A place where people of many cultures, languages, and religions live side by side, each keeping their own traditions.
Attacking an enemy first because you believe it is getting ready to attack you.
An agreement between countries to defend each other: if one is attacked, the others help.
A company in a sector the country needs in order to function, such as energy, oil, or water.
The public institution that manages a country's currency and sets its basic interest rate.
When the central bank decides on its own, without taking orders from the president or ministers.
A tax on products that come from another country. It makes imported products more expensive.
Factories and companies that make things inside the country itself.
Laws that neither favor nor disadvantage any religion, or people with no religion.
Setting aside a share of places for people from certain racial groups.
A plant or animal whose DNA was changed in a lab, for example to resist pests.
The list of what students must learn in each grade.
When a region leaves the country and becomes an independent country.
A Brazilian community descended from enslaved people who escaped and founded their own villages.
A region's power to make its own decisions without asking the national government for permission.
The group of elected representatives who make the laws and oversee the government.
A rule that stops the same person from governing more than a set number of times or years.
Every adult can vote, and no one can find out who each person voted for.
A vote in which the people decide directly whether to approve a law.
Removing a politician from office before the end of the term they were elected for.
A government where power sits with a few people, without free elections or real opposition.
When different parties or groups take turns in government over time.
An open meeting where residents themselves discuss and vote on decisions.
An organized group that controls crime in an area, often with weapons.
An order that forbids people from being outside at certain hours.
When a doctor helps a very ill person die, at their request, to end their suffering.
Solving problems between countries by talking and negotiating instead of using weapons.
Giving up something you wanted in order to reach an agreement.
The most destructive bombs there are: a single one can wipe out a whole city.
An agreement between countries to reduce or destroy some of their weapons.
Secretly gathering information from another country, such as military or government plans.
Acts that are banned even in war, such as deliberately attacking civilians or torturing prisoners.
Weapons, such as drones, that choose and attack targets on their own, without a person deciding at the moment.
To convince others not to attack by showing that the response would be far worse for them.
An organization that brings together almost every country in the world to try to keep the peace.
Soldiers from several countries sent to help keep things calm after a conflict.
Deliberately trying to destroy an entire people because of their origin, ethnicity, or religion.
Economic penalties against a country, such as banning trade or freezing its money.
Organizations made up of many countries, like the United Nations, to solve problems together.
Countries with great economic and military strength that influence the rest of the world.
Having to always back another country's decisions, even without agreeing.
A written agreement signed by countries, which they commit to honor.
Not taking anyone's side in a war.
A place in another country where a country keeps soldiers, planes, or ships.
A school that teaches in two languages at once.
Someone who feels part of humanity as a whole more than of one particular country.
To take part of the wealth from those who have a lot and give it to those who have little.
When several companies compete for the same customers, which tends to lower prices.
Companies and businesses owned by private individuals, not the government.
Property and money a person leaves to their family when they die.
Running things with the aim of making money, like an ordinary business.
A sum of money the government pays every month to guarantee the basics for living.
A rule that stops public employees from being fired, except in serious cases.
A government program that pays poor families a monthly sum, with some conditions.
Breaking up large estates and handing the land to families who have nowhere to farm.
An association of workers that negotiates pay and rights on behalf of everyone.
A government-owned bank that lends money for infrastructure, businesses, and housing.
A company owned by the government.
When the government decides what, how much, and where to produce, instead of leaving it to the market.
Government programs and actions, such as healthcare, schools, and benefits.
How much of the country's income goes to the government as taxes.
When the government pays part of a company's or industry's costs to help it.
The lowest pay the law allows an employer to give a worker.
Banning by law any increase in a price for a period of time.
When prices rise across the board and money buys less.
Large domestic companies the government chooses to back so they can compete globally.
Digital money not issued by any government, such as Bitcoin.
A system where the government decides production and prices instead of companies.
A system where prices and production are set by free buying and selling between people and companies.
Government rules about how companies may operate.
A period when the economy shrinks, businesses sell less, and unemployment rises.
The price of borrowing money. High rates make loans dearer and slow spending.
How much the country's currency is worth compared with others, like the dollar.
Buying products made in another country.
Buying and selling between countries without extra taxes or barriers.
The whole world working as one market, with no barriers between countries.
When several countries' economies become tied together through lots of trade and investment.
Money from foreign companies or people put into businesses inside the country.
The whole production path of something essential, from raw materials to the final product.
A company that operates in many countries at once.
When a country depends little on others to produce what it needs.
Objects or images tied to a religion, such as crosses, statues of saints, or verses.
When a country declares one religion as the official religion of the state.
The ideas of right and wrong that guide laws and life in society.
A family made up of a father, a mother, and children, usually joined by marriage.
How a person sees themselves: as a man, a woman, or otherwise, which may or may not match the sex they were born with.
Short for lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender people.
Ending a pregnancy before the baby can be born.
Offering sexual services in exchange for money.
Ways of speaking and writing that avoid marking words as masculine or feminine.
Having more than one romantic relationship at a time, with everyone's knowledge and consent.
When a country starts producing a lot in factories, with machines.
Computer programs that do tasks that used to need a person thinking, like writing or recognizing images.
Using machines and software to do jobs that people used to do.
A chemical used on crops to kill pests, fungi, or weeds.
Digging minerals, such as gold or iron, out of the ground.
A piece of nature protected by law, where almost nothing can be built or exploited.
Changing parts of DNA, the body's "instruction manual", to fix or alter traits.
The earliest stage of a human being, in the first weeks after conception.
The rise in the planet's average temperature, linked to greenhouse gas pollution.
A small device placed in the brain that connects to computers.
A part or device placed inside the body to change or boost what it can do.
Meat produced in a lab from animal cells, without slaughtering an animal.
Raising animals, such as cattle and pigs, for meat, milk, and leather.
